key_insight: Molecular dynamics shows that in β-Sn, absorbed ⟨c⟩ dislocations can drive $(301)$ twin-boundary faceting, with facet length increasing as more dislocations are absorbed.
engineering_relevance: This mechanism helps explain and potentially control deformation and strengthening behavior in Sn-based solder alloys under dislocation-rich loading.
method: MD simulations of β-Sn twin-boundary/dislocation interactions
Machine-learned interatomic potential used to model atomic-scale defect behavior
Elasticity analysis including disclination character to predict facet length
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simulation results that reproduce experimentally observed faceting trends and show agreement with isotropic elasticity theory only after accounting for the asymmetric twin facet’s disclination character.
watch_item: The conclusions rely on a specific MLIP-driven simulation setup, so transferability to other loading conditions, compositions, or twin geometries should be checked.
paper_title: Dislocation mediated twin boundary faceting in $β$-Sn
